candidate_payload.abstract_text: Stiff-man syndrome (SMS) is a rare autoimmune disorder of the central nervous system associated with autoantibodies to glutamate decarboxylase (GAD). We isolated five brain-reactive human monoclonal antibodies, with reactivity distinct from GAD, from peripheral blood of a patient newly diagnosed with SMS. Two antibodies reacted with both Purkinje cells and ependymal cells, and precipitated an 80-kDa protein from rat neuronal primary cultures, which was also recognized by 12% (3/25) of SMS sera and 13% (2/15) of SMS cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples. The corresponding antigen was identified as 17 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 4 and may represent a possible novel target of autoimmunity in SMS.

autoimmune disease; mass spectrometry 1. introduction stiff-man syndrome (sms) and its variants are rare disorders of the central nervous system characterized by progressive muscle rigidity and superimposed painful spasms (moersch and woltman, 1956). stiffness and spasms are thought to result from a dysfunction of inhibitory g- aminobutyric acid (gaba)ergic neuronal pathways (meinck et al., 1994) . in addition to these two obligatory symptoms, patients may develop a variety of facultative neurological or psychiatric symptoms such as ataxia, retin- opathy or agoraphobia (barker et al., 1998; brown and marsden, 1999; henningsen et al., 1996; tinsley et al., 1997). the etiology and pathogenesis of sms and its variants are unknown. however, since these disorders are frequently associated with other autoimmune diseases like type i diabetes mellitus (bosi et al., 1988; solimena et al., 1988), an autoimmune hypothesis was suggested for sms (blum and jankovic, 1991; young, 1966) . supporting this hypothesis, autoantibodies directed against the gaba-syn- thesizing enzyme, glutamic acid decarboxylase (gad), were identified in the serum and cerebrospinal fluid (csf) of 60 – 80% of sms patients (solimena et al., 1988, 1990) . gad-autoantibody-positive sera from sms patients can inhibit gaba synthesis in vitro (dinkel et al., 1998) , suggesting that gad antibodies may have an implication in gabaergic dysfunction. in sms patients associated with breast cancer, autoantibodies to the 128-kda protein amphi- physin occur in the absence of gad antibodies (folli et al., 1993). one patient with clinical features of sms and media- stinal cancer showed antibodies directed to gephyrin, a cy- tosolic protein concentrated at the postsynaptic membrane of inhibitory synapses. in three other patients without asso- ciated tumors, antibodies to an unknown 80-kda antigen have been reported (darnell et al., 1993; Metadata abstract:
Stiff-man syndrome (SMS) is a rare autoimmune disorder of the central nervous system associated with autoantibodies to glutamate decarboxylase (GAD). We isolated five brain-reactive human monoclonal antibodies, with reactivity distinct from GAD, from peripheral blood of a patient newly diagnosed with SMS. Two antibodies reacted with both Purkinje cells and ependymal cells, and precipitated an 80-kDa protein from rat neuronal primary cultures, which was also recognized by 12% (3/25) of SMS sera and 13% (2/15) of SMS cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples. The corresponding antigen was identified as 17 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 4 and may represent a possible novel target of autoimmunity in SMS.
